title: Entanglement generation in a two-body Schrödinger--Newton model
summary: The Schrödinger--Newton (SN) equation provides a semiclassical framework for the evolution of self-gravitating of massive quantum systems. We propose a two-body Schrödinger--Newton model that separates local nonlinear self-localization from the nonseparable Newtonian pair potential. Analytically, we show that the nonlinear self-field preserves the Schmidt spectrum, whereas direct entanglement generation arises from the nonseparable pair potential. Using numerical simulations in a regularized one-dimensional geometry, we find that entanglement generation depends sensitively on the initial spatial configuration and on the mass ratio. Highly localized, self-bound wavepackets experience minimal entanglement growth during scattering. Spatial delocalization and kinetic dispersion broaden the interaction region, amplifying the entangling power of the pair potential and exciting higher-order spatial modes. For dispersive Gaussian initial states, mass asymmetry shatters the lighter particle, producing Wigner negativity and rapid entanglement growth, whereas stationary SN profiles strongly suppress this effect. Stationary SN profiles isolate the bare pair-potential contribution; dispersive Gaussian initial states inflate it.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the two-body Schrödinger-Newton model, finding that entanglement generation depends on initial spatial configuration and mass ratio, with localized wavepackets suppressing entanglement and dispersive Gaussian states amplifying it, especially under mass asymmetry.
AI.motivation: To understand how self-gravitating quantum systems entangle through the interplay between local nonlinear self-localization (self-field) and nonseparable Newtonian pair potential, and to determine which factors control entanglement generation in the two-body SN model.
AI.method: Analytical derivation showing the nonlinear self-field preserves Schmidt spectrum while pair potential generates entanglement; numerical simulations in a regularized one-dimensional geometry exploring varying initial spatial configurations and mass ratios.
AI.result: Entanglement generation is highly sensitive to initial spatial configuration and mass ratio. Self-bound wavepackets suppress entanglement; dispersive Gaussian states amplify it. Mass asymmetry shatters lighter particles, producing Wigner negativity and rapid entanglement growth, while stationary SN profiles isolate the bare pair-potential contribution.
AI.conclusion: Stationary SN profiles suppress entanglement and isolate the bare pair-potential contribution, whereas dispersive Gaussian initial states inflate it, highlighting the importance of initial state preparation in semiclassical gravity experiments.

title: Practical Log-Depth Quantum State Preparation and Circuit Verification via Tree Tensor Network Compilation
summary: Matrix product states provide efficient classical descriptions of quantum systems that may be useful as reference states for quantum algorithms such as quantum phase estimation and quantum-selected configuration interaction. Shallow circuit constructions for loading matrix product states onto quantum computers is necessary for this to be practical on near-term hardware. We present a decomposition of matrix product states to log-depth quantum circuits via a simple tree tensor network renormalisation procedure. Our method exposes an explicit parameter which can be used to trade a small amount of fidelity for large savings in circuit depth. We extend this decomposition to the case of matrix product operators allowing us to construct log-depth and ancilla-free circuits to calculate overlaps of the form $\left |\langleφ|U|ψ\rangle\right |^2$. In particular, we demonstrate an interpretation of these circuits as \emph{verifier circuits} with application to circuit-level device calibration.

AI.tldr: Presents a log-depth quantum circuit decomposition for matrix product states via tree tensor network renormalization, enabling fidelity-depth tradeoffs and ancilla-free overlap calculations for quantum device calibration.
AI.motivation: Matrix product states are useful reference states for quantum algorithms (e.g., quantum phase estimation) but require shallow circuits for near-term quantum hardware implementation.
AI.method: Decomposes MPS into log-depth quantum circuits using a tree tensor network renormalization procedure, with an explicit tunable parameter for fidelity-depth tradeoff. Extends the decomposition to matrix product operators for ancilla-free overlap calculation.
AI.result: Achieves log-depth circuit constructions for loading MPS onto quantum computers, and ancilla-free circuits for computing overlaps of the form |⟨φ|U|ψ⟩|², interpreted as verifier circuits for device calibration.
AI.conclusion: The log-depth decomposition makes MPS loading practical for near-term quantum hardware, and the verifier circuit interpretation provides a new approach to circuit-level device calibration.

title: Machine Learning Approaches to Building Quantum Circuits for Sets of Matrices
summary: Machine learning nowadays becomes a useful instrument in many subjects. In this paper we use interpretable machine learning to build quantum algorithm. By studying the parameters of the machine learning algorithm we were able to construct universal shortest analytic quantum algorithm for arbitrary diagonal matrix of any size.

AI.motivation: Machine learning has become useful across many fields, and the authors aim to leverage interpretable machine learning techniques to advance quantum algorithm design.

AI.result: The authors successfully constructed a universal shortest analytic quantum algorithm applicable to arbitrary diagonal matrices of any size.
AI.conclusion: Interpretable machine learning can be effectively used to construct quantum algorithms, demonstrated by the creation of a universal shortest analytic quantum algorithm for diagonal matrices.
